items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about Hank (Mancini) and a fortune teller who mentions the name 'Green' (Joe Green). The interviewee does not claim a personal relationship with Joe Green, only that they are aware of the anecdote.

ctx.x: He and Pete Rugolo are great friends who wrote for, one of the arrangers who wrote for Stan Kenton in the early years, Pete Rugolo, David Rose and there’s somebody else and Mancini. They were all in Hawaii with their wives, like vacationing, in the early years. And Hank went into a fortune teller, I mean just off the street, the four of them. Everybody else went first and then Hank. And she says, “I see a great deal of success in your life,” she says, “and in your former life your name was Green.”
Which is Verdi, you know, which is Italian for Green. So we call him Joe Green.

Two weeks later, Hank was, and Hank told me this story, two weeks later he was in Los Angeles at Universal City and he was a ghost writer, and he was getting like B movies like “The Creature from the Black Lagoon” and all of that. And Blake Edwards was walking by him and he says, “Hank” he says, “I got a new series starting,” he said, “I’m going to call you next week.” He called him next week — “Mr. Lucky.” And the rest is history. © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-
